solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Toes treated with proteins for internal displacement

indicators.note: material that is treated is processed and changed, so the letters before and after are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foot condition handled with protein supplements, apparently to cure some inner upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTEROPTOSIS is a medical term: the bowel has dropped from its normal place, which is why 'internal displacement' fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteroptosis is the downward sagging of the intestines inside the abdomen, a displacement of an organ within the body.

clue.text: Enrich stews with power of kidneys

indicators.note: to stew is to cook slowly in a pot, mixing things up, so the word before is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Recipe advice: kidneys add strength and richness to a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enrich stews' reads like a cookery tip, but stews is a verb acting on enrich, and the power letter joins the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephric is the adjective relating to the kidneys, from Greek nephros, kidney.

clue.text: Like tripe or trifle mum swallowed

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so one word goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: to toy with something is to trifle with it
mum, as in 'keep mum', is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A disgusted diner: whether the tripe or the trifle, Mum ate it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe and trifle look like food, but tripe means rubbish here and trifle is a verb; mum means silence, not mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is nonsense, and tripe is slang for worthless rubbish, so something toshy is like tripe.

clue.text: Old coat mostly turned up with nothing below collar

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top, backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the garment's name is dropped

parts.note: a tabard is a sleeveless tunic worn over armour, a garment of the past
nought looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An antique coat with its lapels turned up and nothing worn under the collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' places the O beneath the rest, which in a down entry puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabato was a stiff, wide lace collar of the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Aforetimes, quantity of paper in production

parts.note: onst is an old dialect form of once, meaning formerly
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Back in the day, a pile of paper went into production.
explanation.walkthrough: ONST is a Chambers dialect spelling of once; Azed draws freely on such words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant or process that is onstream has started operating, so it is actively in production.

clue.text: Arbitrator interrupting meal — it's not allowed on Jewish menu

definitions.text: it's not allowed on Jewish menu

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: tea is an evening or afternoon meal in Britain
a referee arbitrates disputes

explanation.surface: A referee barges into dinner and declares a dish forbidden under Jewish dietary rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can mean an early evening meal, not just the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Terefa (treif) is food that is not kosher, which Jewish dietary law forbids eating.

clue.text: Old poet, good on love, cause of global upheaval but not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the preceding phrase's answer is left off

parts.note: the coronavirus pandemic turned the world upside down from 2020

explanation.surface: A classical poet who wrote well about love is linked to a worldwide crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Puzzle published at New Year 2022, when the pandemic was the obvious global upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet whose Ars Amatoria and Amores made him antiquity's great authority on love.

clue.text: Fancy urns lifted low parlour, bright (7, two words)

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine or embellish, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting a word makes it read upwards, back to front

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Decorative urns raised up in a dimly lit parlour that is nonetheless bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective for the parlour, but it is the verb for what cows do.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunroom is a glazed sitting room built to let in plenty of sunlight, so a bright parlour.

clue.text: Gardenin' has disinterred this local onion, red

indicators.note: disinterred means dug up, and digging turns things over into a new order
the first word is said to contain both the answer and the colour, so the colour is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, its dropped g giving it a dialect flavour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dialect-speaking gardener digs up a red onion.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of GARDENIN equal the answer plus RED, so removing RED and rearranging the rest gives INGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingan is a Scots and northern dialect word for onion, hence local.

clue.text: Man admits love with mum — one's predictions are distinctly 'earthy'

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word for man holds the others inside

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A man lets in love along with his mother, and his forecasts are rather down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earthy' in quotes points to the Greek ge, earth, in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A geomant practises geomancy, divination from patterns of earth or dots, so his prophecies are literally earth-based.

clue.text: Cop deployed against mobs, bung deviously secreted in paunch?

indicators.note: secreted in means hidden inside, so one piece is tucked into another

parts.note: gaster is an old word for the belly

indicators.note: acting deviously means taking a crooked route, so the letters go astray from their order

parts.note: taken as written; a bung is also slang for a bribe

explanation.surface: A bent policeman hides a bribe under his belly.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a bung is a bribe, which feeds the picture of a corrupt cop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangbuster is a police officer or agent who breaks up organised criminal gangs.

clue.text: Nonsense

parts.note: surface reading: the plain meaning, foolish talk
setter's reading: this is the competition word, printed with a bare definition for solvers to write their own clue

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own cryptic clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk or writing, a direct synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Dog (origin unspecified) needing shampoo, rear half first

indicators.note: putting the back half in front swaps the two halves of the word round

parts.note: soap is what you shampoo with

explanation.surface: A dog of unknown breed that badly needs a wash, starting from the back end.
explanation.walkthrough: The breed is the Lhasa apso; '(origin unspecified)' tells you to drop Lhasa, its place of origin in Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Apso is the Lhasa apso without the name of its Tibetan home city, a small long-haired breed of dog.

clue.text: You may find gardener is transplanting red one?

definitions.text: You may find gardener is transplanting red one?

indicators.note: you may find the answer among the letters only by rearranging what remains of them
transplanting moves something out of where it was, so the colour is lifted out of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener moving a red-flowered shrub might be handling one of these.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RED out of GARDENER IS and the remaining seven letters rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also describes a gardener at work with the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Seringa is the mock orange (philadelphus), a garden shrub a gardener might well transplant.

clue.text: Major church chap introducing doctor coming in to cure

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man or fellow

indicators.note: coming in to something means entering it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to cure is to heal
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A man brings in a physician who arrives to treat a patient at a big church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' just puts CAT at the front of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, containing the bishop's throne.

clue.text: Once bitten and angry, one disposed of pet, heartless

indicators.note: disposed of means got rid of, so those letters are removed from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
an means one, as in 'an apple'

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of pet

explanation.surface: Once bitten and angry, someone got rid of their heartless pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an obsolete word: GRYPT is a Spenserian form meaning bitten or gripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Grypt is an archaic Spenserian past participle meaning pierced or bitten, so 'once' signals the old usage.

clue.text: The heavens, timeless void about one

indicators.note: the suffix -less means without, so the usual abbreviation for time is dropped

parts.note: void and empty both mean containing nothing
re means about or concerning
an means one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: The sky as an eternal emptiness surrounding us all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless void' looks like a single poetic phrase for space, which fits the definition, but timeless is the instruction to remove T.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the highest heaven, or the sky itself, in ancient and poetic cosmology.

clue.text: Leafy outgrowth, tender, round flower's extremity

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: fond and tender both mean affectionate

indicators.note: an extremity is the far end, so only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of flower

explanation.surface: A delicate leaf curls round the end of a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The R sits inside FOND to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A frond is the large divided leaf of a fern or palm, a leafy outgrowth of the plant.

clue.text: One of five I begot, developing differently (6, two words)

indicators.note: developing differently means growing into another form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent of quintuplets notes that one of their children turned out unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of five' reads as one child among five, but it is one of the five toes on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The big toe is one of the five digits on each human foot.

clue.text: Large reptile prowling in Aligarh?

indicators.note: a prowling animal roams restlessly about, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written; Aligarh is a city in northern India

explanation.surface: A big reptile on the prowl in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is fanciful: gharials live in northern Indian rivers, so one near Aligarh is plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The gharial is a long-snouted crocodilian of Indian rivers, growing to several metres.

clue.text: Some sharks Jock's to prepare, unusually large

parts.note: mak is the Scots form of make, and to make a meal is to prepare it
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sets about preparing some outsized sharks.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, so 'Jock's' signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Makos are fast, large sharks of the genus Isurus, so the plural fits 'some sharks'.

clue.text: School's head called in by governing body showing discernment?

indicators.note: someone called in by a body is brought inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a senate is a governing council, as of a university or state

indicators.note: 'head' keeps only the first letter of 'School'

parts.note: the first letter of school

explanation.surface: A headteacher summoned before the governors shows good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that discernment here means perception through the senses rather than wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensate means perceiving through the senses, so able to discern things physically.

clue.text: Coach taken in by rich Arabs

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Wealthy Arabs ride in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach is a vehicle here, not a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chara is short for charabanc, an old open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Put fresh front on shift, turned-up iron plugged in

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: to shift is to move fast, to race

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a piece up makes it read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Fresh facing on an electric iron that has been switched on for a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift is slang for moving at speed, as in 'that car can really shift'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reface a building or object is to give it a new outer surface, a fresh front.

clue.text: Sign of cold weather in part of mid- April? One'll need a second coat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the middle letters of April are PRI, and part of that is PR
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Frost appears in mid-April, so you will need another coat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second coat' sounds like outerwear against the cold, but it is a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Primer is the first layer of paint applied to a surface, which then needs a further coat on top.

clue.text: Change address for number in former province

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: reame is an obsolete spelling of realm, a kingdom or province
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Moving house and changing your postal address in an old province.
explanation.walkthrough: Address here means the name you call someone by, not where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: To rename is to change the name by which something is called or addressed.

clue.text: Risk creating gaffe, avoiding motorway initially

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so those letters are left out at the start

parts.note: a gaffe is a mistake
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, read as MI, and initially places it at the front

explanation.surface: Driving is risky when you make a blunder by missing the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; in crosswords its 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is what you put at risk in a bet, and to stake is to risk it.

clue.text: Draw on Press Association for material for paper

parts.note: to tap a resource is to draw on it
PA is the Press Association, the UK news agency

explanation.surface: A newspaper uses the news agency's material for its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Material for paper suggests copy for a newspaper, but it is the bark used to make tapa cloth and paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tappa is the inner bark of the paper mulberry, from which a paper-like tapa cloth is made.

clue.text: SA creature, not heading for the Cape?

indicators.note: not heading means without a front, so the leading letters are cut off

parts.note: a cape is a headland, also called a foreland
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African animal is not making for the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the Cape' reads as a direction, but FOR is the head to drop from a word for cape.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: During normal working days we make out without money

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are reshuffled
without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: On ordinary weekdays we just about scrape by with no cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make out' reads as get by, but out is the signal for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A-week is a Chambers adverb meaning on weekdays, in the course of the working week.

clue.text: Some bracken from Far East flourishing among lakes (9, two words)

indicators.note: among puts one piece in the middle of the other

parts.note: tarns are small mountain lakes

indicators.note: flourishing means waving about with a flourish, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Bracken from the Orient thrives beside lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far East' looks like a place, but splits into FAR and the compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tara fern is the New Zealand name for bracken, whose rhizomes were eaten by Maori.

clue.text: Settled in a form of worship — any absent?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: absent means missing, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a litany is a form of prayer with responses
taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling into a church service and wondering whether anyone is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Alit is an old past tense of alight, used of a bird coming to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is a past tense of alight, to come down and settle on something.

clue.text: Hand washer applied to edge of face for shave?

indicators.note: 'edge of' keeps only the last letter of 'face'

parts.note: the outer letter of face, here the end one
Pontius Pilate washed his hands of Jesus's fate

explanation.surface: Splashing your hands then your face before a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applied to' places the hand washer after the edge letter. Definition is a verb with a question mark, since depilation is broader than shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To epilate is to remove hair from the body, and shaving is one way of doing so.

clue.text: Vegetables planted among the hippeastrums

indicators.note: planted among means set within, so the letters sit inside the word that follows

parts.note: the run of letters inside the plant name

explanation.surface: A gardener has put vegetables in among the bulbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippeastrums are the large-flowered bulbs often sold as amaryllis.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas are a common vegetable, the seeds of a climbing legume.

clue.text: Borough, it's origin found in sprawling hamlet

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other
something sprawling spreads out untidily, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the first letter of the definition word, borough

explanation.surface: A London borough traces its beginnings to a straggling village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' (as printed, for 'its') refers back to the definition, whose first letter is the piece placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is a borough of south London, home to Lambeth Palace.

clue.text: Prince maybe with bird, English, on deck relaxing, not plunging?

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

indicators.note: relaxing means loosening up, so the letters loosen into another order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prince relaxes on the deck of a ship with a bird and an Englishman, not diving in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not plunging' looks like not diving overboard, but refers to a plunging neckline.
explanation.definitionFit: A halternecked top is held by a strap round the neck, covering the chest rather than having a low-cut plunging neckline.
